definitions.explanation: Fine particles of matter that accumulate on surfaces or float in the air. Also used figuratively for impurities or worldly attachments.

examples.japanese: {棚|たな}の{上|うえ}に{塵|ちり}が{積|つ}もっている。
examples.english: Dust has accumulated on top of the shelf.

examples.japanese: {塵|ちり}も{積|つ}もれば{山|やま}となる。
examples.english: Even dust, when piled up, becomes a mountain. (Many a little makes a mickle.)

examples.japanese: {風|かぜ}が{吹|ふ}くと{塵|ちり}が{舞|ま}い{上|あ}がって{目|め}に{入|はい}りそうになった。
examples.english: When the wind blew, the dust swirled up and nearly got in my eyes.

notes:
PROVERB:
{塵|ちり}も{積|つ}もれば{山|やま}となる — "Even dust piles up into a mountain." A well-known proverb meaning that small amounts accumulate into something significant.

USAGE:
{塵|ちり} refers to very fine particles — finer than {埃|ほこり} (dust, in everyday speech). In everyday conversation, {埃|ほこり} is more common for household dust. {塵|ちり} appears more in literary contexts and set phrases. The pair {塵|ちり}{芥|あくた} means "dust and rubbish" — worthless things.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {塵|ちり}が{積|つ}もる: dust accumulates
- {塵|ちり}が{舞|ま}う: dust swirls
- {塵|ちり}ひとつない: not a speck of dust
- {塵|ちり}{芥|あくた}: dust and rubbish, worthless things

SIMILAR WORDS:
{塵|ちり} is literary and refers to very fine particles. {埃|ほこり} (dust) is the everyday word for household dust. ゴミ (garbage, trash) is broader and refers to waste in general.
